title: Small-Bowel Obstruction: Step-Ladder Pattern and Transition Point
subject: Radiological Signs
preview: Dilated small bowel loops and multiple air–fluid levels can suggest small-bowel obstruction.
quickRevision: Dilated small bowel loops and multiple air–fluid levels can suggest small-bowel obstruction.
Prior abdominal surgery raises the likelihood of adhesions, but hernia and malignancy remain important differentials.
Severe persistent pain, fever, peritoneal signs and rising lactate may raise concern for compromised bowel.

sections.title: Recognize the pattern
points: Dilated small bowel loops and multiple air–fluid levels can suggest small-bowel obstruction.
CT can help identify a transition point, cause, strangulation or ischemic complications.

sections.title: What this finding does—and does not—mean
points: Prior abdominal surgery raises the likelihood of adhesions, but hernia and malignancy remain important differentials.
Severe persistent pain, fever, peritoneal signs and rising lactate may raise concern for compromised bowel.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Plain radiographic patterns are not sufficiently specific to identify the precise cause or exclude ischemia.

quiz.question: What does a CT transition point help localize?
quiz.explanation: The site of intestinal obstruction. CT can help identify a transition point, cause, strangulation or ischemic complications.
